q-138492.name: Question 1
q-138492.problem:
For the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
q-138492.worked_solution:
For an "almost" zero $m\times n$ matrix with non-zero entries 

$$
{\sigma }_{1},\,{\sigma }_{2},\,…,\,{\sigma }_{r}
$$

on the main diagonal, the corresponding pseudoinverse is the "almost" zero $n\times m$ matrix with entries 

$$
{\sigma }_{1}^{-1},\,{\sigma }_{2}^{-1},\,…,\,{\sigma }_{r}^{-1}
$$

on the main diagonal.

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{+} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{4}^{-1} & \,\,\,0 & 0 \\ \,\,0 & \,{2}^{-1} & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

For the matrix A=[400200], find the pseudoinverse A+.

a
12[200010]
b
14[100020]
c
14[200010]
d
[100020]
e
12[100020]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For an "almost" zero m×n matrix with non-zero entries

σ1,σ2,…,σr

on the main diagonal, the corresponding pseudoinverse is the "almost" zero n×m matrix with entries

σ1−1,σ2−1,…,σr−1

on the main diagonal.

Therefore, we obtain

A+=[400200]+=[4−10002−10]=14[100020].

q-138489.problem:
For the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
q-138489.worked_solution:
For an "almost" zero $m\times n$ matrix with non-zero entries 

$$
{\sigma }_{1},\,{\sigma }_{2},\,…,\,{\sigma }_{r}
$$

on the main diagonal, the corresponding pseudoinverse is the "almost" zero $n\times m$ matrix with entries 

$$
{\sigma }_{1}^{-1},\,{\sigma }_{2}^{-1},\,…,\,{\sigma }_{r}^{-1}
$$

on the main diagonal.

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{+} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{2}^{-1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{-1} & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

For the matrix A=[200200], find the pseudoinverse A+.

a
12[100100]
b
14[100010]
c
12[−1000−10]
d
12[100010]

14[100100]

EXPLANATION

For an "almost" zero m×n matrix with non-zero entries

σ1,σ2,…,σr

on the main diagonal, the corresponding pseudoinverse is the "almost" zero n×m matrix with entries

σ1−1,σ2−1,…,σr−1

on the main diagonal.

Therefore, we obtain

A+=[200200]+=[2−10002−10]=12[100010].

q-138494.name: Question 3
q-138494.problem:
For the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
q-138494.worked_solution:
For an "almost" zero $m\times n$ matrix with non-zero entries 

$$
{\sigma }_{1},\,{\sigma }_{2},\,…,\,{\sigma }_{r}
$$

on the main diagonal, the corresponding pseudoinverse is the "almost" zero $n\times m$ matrix with entries 

$$
{\sigma }_{1}^{-1},\,{\sigma }_{2}^{-1},\,…,\,{\sigma }_{r}^{-1}
$$

on the main diagonal.

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & ={[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 8 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{+} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{5}^{-1} & \,\,\,0 & 0 \\ \,\,0 & \,{8}^{-1} & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{40}[\begin{aligned}8 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

For an "almost" zero m×n matrix with non-zero entries

σ1,σ2,…,σr

on the main diagonal, the corresponding pseudoinverse is the "almost" zero n×m matrix with entries

σ1−1,σ2−1,…,σr−1

on the main diagonal.

Therefore, we obtain

A+=[500800]+=[5−10008−10]=140[800050].

q-138490.name: Question 4
q-138490.problem:
For the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
q-138490.worked_solution:
For an "almost" zero $m\times n$ matrix with non-zero entries 

$$
{\sigma }_{1},\,{\sigma }_{2},\,…,\,{\sigma }_{r}
$$

on the main diagonal, the corresponding pseudoinverse is the "almost" zero $n\times m$ matrix with entries 

$$
{\sigma }_{1}^{-1},\,{\sigma }_{2}^{-1},\,…,\,{\sigma }_{r}^{-1}
$$

on the main diagonal.

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{+} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{1}^{-1} & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

For the matrix A=[1000], find the pseudoinverse A+.

a

[0001]

EXPLANATION

For an "almost" zero m×n matrix with non-zero entries

σ1,σ2,…,σr

on the main diagonal, the corresponding pseudoinverse is the "almost" zero n×m matrix with entries

σ1−1,σ2−1,…,σr−1

on the main diagonal.

Therefore, we obtain

A+=[1000]+=[1−1000]=[1000].

q-138488.name: Question 5
q-138488.problem:
For the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}],$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
q-138488.worked_solution:
For an "almost" zero $m\times n$ matrix with non-zero entries 

$$
{\sigma }_{1},\,{\sigma }_{2},\,…,\,{\sigma }_{r}
$$

on the main diagonal, the corresponding pseudoinverse is the "almost" zero $n\times m$ matrix with entries 

$$
{\sigma }_{1}^{-1},\,{\sigma }_{2}^{-1},\,…,\,{\sigma }_{r}^{-1}
$$

on the main diagonal.

Therefore, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & ={[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{+} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{4}^{-1} & 0 \\ 0 & {3}^{-1} \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

For the matrix A=[400030], find the pseudoinverse A+.

a
112[004003]
b
112[−400300]
c

112[300040]

EXPLANATION

For an "almost" zero m×n matrix with non-zero entries

σ1,σ2,…,σr

on the main diagonal, the corresponding pseudoinverse is the "almost" zero n×m matrix with entries

σ1−1,σ2−1,…,σr−1

on the main diagonal.

Therefore, we obtain

A+=[400030]+=[4−1003−100]=112[300400].

q-138533.name: Question 6
q-138533.problem:
$$
U=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
q-138533.worked_solution:
If $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ then the pseudoinverse of $A$ is given by

$$
V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T},
$$

where ${Σ}^{+}$ is the pseudoinverse of $Σ.$

First, notice that

$$
V=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{Σ}^{+}=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{U}^{T}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{2} \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & =V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{2} \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{2} \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{2} \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-138520.name: Question 7
q-138520.problem:
$$
U=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
q-138520.worked_solution:
If $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ then the pseudoinverse of $A$ is given by

$$
V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T},
$$

where ${Σ}^{+}$ is the pseudoinverse of $Σ.$

First, notice that

$$
V=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{Σ}^{+}=\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{U}^{T}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & =V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-138495.problem:
$$
U=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{10} & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
q-138495.worked_solution:
If $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ then the pseudoinverse of $A$ is given by

$$
V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T},
$$

where ${Σ}^{+}$ is the pseudoinverse of $Σ.$

First, notice that

$$
V=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,{Σ}^{+}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{U}^{T}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & =V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{20}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

VΣ+UT,
